steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This is far enough. We're already at the wakemen camp.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Your sister roused me from my slumber. You could always return me to it with your own flames, if you want.
Reed!
A golden-haired Perro leaps off the back of a burdenbeast and rushes toward the red dragon.
The burdenbeast is dragging an improvised cart with numerous long wooden boxes stacked upon it.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: —Brigid?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What are you doing here? Are those—

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Coffins?!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Yeah, coffins. Nemos said to bring 'em to the wakemen. Are they still in the ruins?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Say, is there someone with you? I can smell that same burning stink, and I could swear I heard you talking just now—

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, I'm alone.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: These are...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Dead folks.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: The type who'd pull their own arms out of their sockets to bite at their imaginary enemies if you grabbed their hand. Along with the poor wretches they tore to pieces.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: And Theo. Nemos found him in the end. He...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: It's almost like this was the natural order of things. The bonfires will be burnin' brightest when night falls on Samhain...
The red dragon looks towards Na Saoirsí, and sees a faint shadow in the distance, painting the silhouette of purple flames.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: We'll be out of coffins if this keeps up.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I hope Brigid made it out of the city. And that the mist in the woods is thin enough for her to follow the trail...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Blast it, Culann left a few unused weapons in his house. I can't let anyone see them.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: And this fuel... explosives? Her Highness Loughshinny might find a use for them.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No, what's the point when every servant in the citadel has already been afflicted by the purple flames? Besides, the greedy red dragon has already sent them away.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Almost as if... she's preparing for a showdown with Her Highness.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Or... setting a trap?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Rory? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: You're... Nemos.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Yes, I'm going through Culann's effects. If this isn't urgent, could I ask you to—

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Traitor.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Have you gone mad?!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Oh, silly me. Of course you have. We all have.

steps.name: Brooding Resident
steps.text: Traitor—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I... I still can't bring myself to kill them. Even if they might as well be dead already.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Ha. Hahahah...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'd better drag this fellow back home. Could do without the unwanted attention.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Nemos?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: D-Don't mind me, I'll be on my way.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: What's that in your hand?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Oh, nothing. Now, if you'll excuse me—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: That necklace. It was a gift from Niels to Emma.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I-I gave her bread! That's way more valuable than jewelry in times like these! She gave it to me!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Did she now? A necklace she never takes off?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I-It's none of your business!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Nemos? You stayed behind? I thought all the Dublinners left the city!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Don't tell me you're one of those living statues now, who refuse to move or talk?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I might be soon. Why did you bring them up?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Samhain begins tonight. So I went through the houses of the missing people, and found plenty of good stuff for the party tonight!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: ...Samhain? Party?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: About Culann—well, he was already on his last legs by then, and I didn't really...

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Let's not talk about that! Look at all this stuff! It'll be a night to remember!
The woman shows Nemos her bag, revealing a bottle of curded cystymilk, a few long-since-sprouted potatoes, and several bare bones.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Just wait for me, Nemos, Culann... we'll have a fantastic Samhain...
Only when the woman has already disappeared around a corner does Nemos remember who she is: a villager who once lived on the outskirts of Na Saoirsí.
Two years ago, the Victorians took her father away while investigating Dublinn. The autumn harvest had just ended, and she had been preparing to celebrate the harvest festival.
What Loughshinny hears about the situation in the city exceeds her wildest imagination.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I must go back. Now.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Wait for me. I'll come with once I've delivered these folks to the wakemen.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Are you sure about this, Brigid?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It's dangerous in the city. If I fail... there may be no survivors.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: True, but I still gotta go.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Because it wasn't like this before.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: The cityfolk never had much to spare, but they always had a cup of water for me when I delivered their letters.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: They didn't see me as one of their own, but didn't walk away with a sneer when I told them nomad legends either. They listened.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: And they definitely didn't bite, claw, and punch at people like they do these days. Like the walking dead straight from a story.

spans.text: didn't bite, claw, and punch at people like they do these days. Like the walking dead straight from a story.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Who will the nomads deliver letters for, if the city dies for real?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Moran?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: The second shipment of bodies has arrived from Na Saoirsí. I must make the preparations.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: At this rate, it won't be long until the third, fourth, or more.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Are we really going to ignore it?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: As I've told you many times, the wakemen do not take sides. It is not our decision to make.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Are the Na Saoirsíans not Tarans too? Why are we standing on the side watching, when the Taran capital is marching towards destruction?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: I know you came back with the red dragon. You fear she will meet the same fate as Labhréathach.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: But we were the ones to send Labhréathach to his doom.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: We are descended from the priests that once officiated the ceremonies of Tara's royal palace.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Our ancestors, moved by Labhréathach's plea, welcomed him back into the palace when Ailill's stance was ambivalent.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: The flames of death that spread through the plains of Tara were only extinguished seven days after his death, when our ancestors finally returned his fire to him.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: They then left the palace of their own accord, going into self-exile on Labhréathach's former pastures, so as to never forget the lesson. And thus, the wakemen were born.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: But Reed isn't Labhréathach, and history is not a cycle that repeats itself endlessly.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: If it were, Reed would have already died in that citadel.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Even her tyrant of a sister was the one to free Tara from Victorian rule.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Fates are often alike, but always differ where it matters most.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: 'Fates are often alike, but always differ where it matters most.'

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: What a wonderful tagline for the cover of the book. Surely this one is destined for the best-seller charts.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Assuming, of course, that you are ever able to finish the story.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: I've never intended to profit off it.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Oh, you will. If not in money, then in fame.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: The basis of the story, where it happened... There are more than enough reasons this isn't my story to tell.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Besides, what happens next?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: That's what I wanted to ask. Did Loughshinny go back?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: From this point on, what I've seen, what I believe, and what I've said all contradict one another. Which is why I've lost sight of the ending.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Feel free to take up the challenge, if you're up to it. Give this dance between the dragon and her reflection whatever ending you please.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Oh? Is it all the same if I tell it myself?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Of course, ma'am. As you will it—
The writer raises his mug, which is almost empty now, and toasts the woman before him.
Once again, he swallows the bitter brew, half-expecting the sweet aftertaste that he knows will never come.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Did I spook you? You got so polite all of a sudden. It makes me feel impertinent for even pressing the question.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: No. But I must make it abundantly clear that everything we have discussed until now is no more than idle chatter. You understand, don't you?
The woman sits straight and does not say a word. The writer can only attempt to guess whether she is still smiling through the shadows.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: Well? What are you waiting for? I've nearly finished my drink.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: I've fallen into the same conundrum as you.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: If this is as far as both your references and your imagination go, how could I possibly put the red dragon's ultimate fate to paper?

spans.text: If this is as far as both your references and your imagination go, how could
possibly put the red dragon's ultimate fate to paper?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: I've already said all I'm able to. I refuse to give this story an entirely fictional end, one that not even I could believe in. Even if the alternative is that there is no ending.

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: If you don't have an answer either, then no need to waste your time here. Leave while it's still early.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Is this because you do not remember, do not understand, or is it because you wish you never knew, never understood?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: —What?

steps.name: Writer
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: You've never 'lost sight of the ending.' It would be more appropriate to say that your eyes have become clouded by too many 'creative liberties'. Shall I recount them for you?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Treasures leading people into the darkness.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Culann dragging the statue to the square by himself.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: And virtually everything related to the dark mist in the woods: from the rejection of Brigid, to the food carts returning to the city on their own, to Loughshinny becoming lost in the woods, to The Brigadier and Eblana's meeting in the city.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: If these 'creative liberties' have created the contradictions in your mind, then it is my responsibility to set them on a path towards the ending.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Shall I supplement the story with my own observations?

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: I'll take that as a yes.

steps.name: Mysterious Woman
steps.text: Perhaps they will lead you to a conclusion you can be satisfied with.
